comparison: Perfect agreement on bifurcation geometry quantification (C81-C87). Both recognize the preservation of average angles but increased deviation metrics, and both support the additive phenotype in triple mutants as evidence for independent guidance roles.

Perfect agreement on mechanistic speculation (C110-C114). Both acknowledge these as reasonable working hypotheses about direct vs. indirect mechanisms that require future investigation. OpenEval explicitly marks as UNCERTAIN/speculative, while peer reviewers implicitly accept as appropriate discussion.
Perfect agreement on wild-type baseline observations (C29-C30). Both accept these descriptive observations of normal DRG axon development without question.

Strong agreement on comparative mutant analysis (C54-C74). Both strongly support the comprehensive analysis showing distinct trajectories and additive phenotypes. Peer reviewers particularly laud the 'sophisticated triple mutant analysis' that OpenEval also identifies as providing strong evidence.

Strong agreement on DRG origin of misprojections (C38-C47, with C6 also in peer result). Both support the genetic lineage tracing evidence. OpenEval notes the scientific rigor in acknowledging incomplete Cre activity; peer reviewers praise the 'Cre-based approaches.'

Strong agreement on Ntn1 loss causing DRG axon misprojections (C5, C31-C37). Both support the converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'axons outside the DREZ in the Ntn1 mutants' with 'compelling axonal labeling and quantification.'

Strong agreement on receptor-mediated phenotypes (C88-C99). Both support that ligand and receptor mutants show parallel phenotypes, confirming bona fide signaling pathways. Peer reviewers note this provides 'additional confirmation of the requirement for both guidance pathways.'

Strong agreement on Ntn1's temporal and mechanistic role (C102-C108, C115). Both support the timing at E10.5, dorsal trajectory, and distinction between guidance vs. bifurcation. Peer reviewers accept these conclusions about 'precise consequences of the loss of each guidance factor.'

Agreement on cellular mechanism speculation (C133-C140). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN/speculative; peer reviewers implicitly accept as reasonable future directions, with Reviewer 3 noting the paper 'provides the foundation for future studies.'

Perfect agreement on background/context claims (C1-C2, C12-C22). Both accept these as established knowledge from prior literature without question. These foundational statements set up the rationale for the current study.

Strong agreement on bifurcation preservation (C75-C80, with C7, C48-C50 also in peer result). Both support that guidance pathways don't affect bifurcation itself. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'none of these knockouts affect bifurcation itself but rather the guidance.'

Strong agreement on hypothesis and rationale (C3-C4, C51-C53). Both support the hypothesis of distinct Ntn1 and Slit functions based on different phenotypes. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'Slit and Ntr1 have distinct functions in guidance.'

Strong agreement on multi-factorial guidance model (C100-C101, C116-C127). Both strongly support the overarching conclusion. Peer reviewers state the study 'expands our understanding' and findings are 'very significant and clearly move forward our understanding.'
Agreement on Ntn1 expression background (C23-C28). Both accept the in situ hybridization data and previous literature on Ntn1 expression patterns as appropriate context.

Partial overlap on comparative biology (C130-C131). OpenEval marks broader framework (C128-C132) as UNCERTAIN/speculative; peer reviewers accept zebrafish comparisons as supporting context without challenge.

Agreement on pathway distinction (C119-C122). Both support that Ntn1 and Slit pathways have distinct functions. This subset of claims from OpenEval R8 aligns with peer reviewers' emphasis on 'cooperative and independent function.'

Agreement on single-axon quantitative analysis (C48-C50). Both support the quantitative evidence of guidance defects. Peer result also includes C7 and bifurcation claims (C75-C80), showing broader grouping of single-axon findings.

Partial agreement on working model (C126-C127, C132). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN noting sequential model involves inference beyond direct data. Peer reviewers accept the overall conclusion about multiple mechanisms as part of the broader supported findings.
